newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 9.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- DELAY LOOMS FOR ELECTRONIC 'BIG BANG TWO' AT EXCHANGE

The switch to computerised trading at London's Stock Exchange, a move dubbed as the second 'Big Bang', could be delayed from the scheduled October 20 start. While the Exchange is understood to be concerned that the Crest settlement system will be unable to cope with the extra volume that will be generated, a survey of its members has also shown that at least one big firm is insufficiently prepared.
-- WH SMITH CUTS BACK ON BANKS

WH Smith, the retail group which includes Waterstone's and Virgin Our Price, is to save about 5 million stg from renegotiating its banking facilities. The group is to cut the number of banks its uses from 30 to nine, and has reduced its total of clearing banks from four to just Barclays and NatWest.
-- WAIGEL GIVES PLEDGE ON SINGLE CURRENCY

Theo Waigel, the German finance minister, has said that the timetable for a single European currency should not be changed. The comments, made at the Luxembourg meeting of European finance ministers, were echoed by Dutch prime minister Wim Kok. Waigel, who is said by one Bundesbank council member to be close to a compromise with the central bank on the issue of revaluing gold reserves, said, 'we will stick by what was agreed'.
THE TIMES
-- SAVERS BONUSES TO FUND COST OF MIS-SELLING

Companies involved in the mis-selling of life insurance policies in the 1980s are transferring the costs of a compensation scheme for victims to current life insurance policyholders. The policyholders are facing bonus cuts and reduced returns on their savings as the insurance companies struggle to fund compensation which is estimated to total more than 4 billion stg.
-- GRANADA 'CLOSE' TO YORKSHIRE TV BID

Granada is reported to be 'close' to commencing negotiations on a takeover bid for rival TV company Yorkshire Tyne-Tees Television. A three-month bid moratorium ends on Friday, and Granada, which already holds a 27 per cent stake in YTTV, could make a move as early as this week. United News & Media, which owns the Meridian and Anglian television franchises, has a 15 per cent stake in YTTV.
-- 'AGGRESSIVE' VIRGIN DIRECT CRITICISED

A aggressive marketing campaign from Virgin Direct, which claims that up to 90 per cent of Pep customers are victims of poor investment performance and uncompetitive charges, has been criticised for threatening to bring the fund management industry into disrepute. The campaign aims to persuade holders of existing Peps to transfer their money to Virgin.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GRANDMET FAILS IN BATTLE ROYAL FOR BRAND NAME

Brewery giant GrandMet has lost control of its Smirnoff vodka brand following a legal battle with descendants of the Russian Smirnoff family. An arbitration court in Moscow is understood to have ruled that the trademark belongs to Boris Smirnoff, a KGB officer and a great-grandson of vodka supplier Peter Smirnoff. According to reports in the Russian press, the ruling was made last week but has yet to be made public.
-- DECLINE IN INDUSTRIAL INNOVATION ALARMS CBI

Employers' organisation the Confederation of British Industry is to warn manufacturers on Monday that they face going to the wall unless they invest more in developing products. A report from the CBI will reveal that spending on innovation by British firms was reduced last year, at a time when the lifespan of their established products was falling.
-- NUMBER'S UP FOR CAR JOBS

Consultants KMPG Management have predicted that up to 10,000 jobs and sales of 740 million stg a year will be lost if the government scraps the annual August change on car registration plates. The industry has been pressing the government to scrap the annual scheme in order to even out sales and production requirements, but the report claims that the move would lose 50,000 new car sales a year.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CENTRICA PUTS GAS METER BUSINESS UP FOR SALE

Centrica, the demerged former British Gas supply operation, has put up for sale Quantum, the business responsible for coin and electronic pre-payment gas meters. British Gas Trading, Centrica's main supply arm, has invited offers to buy or run the operation, though the price of any deal is being kept commercial confidential. The move is likely to raise further doubts about the costs of supplying low-income customers in a deregulated domestic energy market.
-- C&W SET FOR KEY ROLE IN CHINA'S FLOAT

US investment bank Goldman Sachs is reported to be preparing plans for the estimated 6 billion stg stock market launch of China Telecom Hong Kong, the company which is expected to be the main vehicle by which China's state telecoms operator China Telecom raises outside capital for development. British group Cable & Wireless could become the lead corporate investor in the group following a deal last week with the Chinese government over C&W's far-eastern subsidiary Hongkong Telecom.
-- RAILTRACK HEADS FOR NEW STORM OVER PAY

Railtrack, the controversial operator of Britain's rail infrastructure, is planning to proceed with long-term bonus schemes which could see its directors and top managers receive free shares worth more than 2 million stg two years from now. The controversial move, which would be forced through without shareholder approval, follows the public row last week with transport secretary John Prescott over Railtrack's profits.
